main_text.p: nus Beneficia divina, ex misericordia Dei, per illas impetramus. Sic ille. Virtus igitur illa non ex Condignitate Operis, sed ex Dei com-placentia beneficia obtinet. Adhuc igitur pi-scati estis in aëre; vox enim hæc, Meritum, per totam Scripturam prorsus muta est; de quo tamen non adeò laboramus, modò Me-riti de Condigno ἀξίως[?] & sensum liquidum ex iis possitis elicere.

p.i: MEritum de Condigno, quoad sensum, Pontificii ex Scripturis variis deducere-conantur; sed frustra.

main_text.head: SECT. III.
I. Scripturarum Clafsis.
main_text.p: CLaffis prima Scripturarum, quam objicit Bellarminus;a Bellarm. lib.5.de Justif.cap.2. Item Coster. Enchirid.de Meritis,c.7 Evidenter (inquit) evincitur ex Scripturis. 1. In locis, in quibus invenitur nomen Dignitatis, ut Apoc. 3. Ambulabant in albis, quia digni. Luc. 20. 35. Digni habebantur seculo illo. 2. Thess. 1. 5. Ut digni habeamini regno Dei. At Pererius vestræ Societatis Jesuita primarius, vel tacentibus nobis, ora vobis obstruet.{b} b Perer.Jes. in Rom. 3. Disp.16. num.ult. Pelagiani dicunt (inquit) Deum non dare primam Gratiam nisi dignis & merentibus. Quibus respondeo; Digni dicuntur gratiam accipere, non tanquam Condigne eam accipere merentes, sed quia per Dei gratiam facti sunt idonei & habiles, & rite præparati ad accipiendam Gratiam.

page.notes: The Greek word after "Meriti de Condigno" is in italic and only partly legible; the reading ἀξίως is uncertain. The page number "15" is doubtful. "deducere-" at the line end has a mark that may be a printed hyphen or a stroke. "SECT. III." is read as a section heading (SECTIO III). The left-hand strip of fragmentary text is the edge of the neighbouring page and is left out. The large initial C is read as a drop cap joined to "Laffis"; the marker after "obstruet." is read as letter b. Italic and roman runs in the first paragraph are approximate.
